title: Vending Machine (optional)

links.title: C++ Core Guidelines (error handling, E section)

hints: Return std::nullopt for 'no valid result' and a plain value (return x;) for success - optional<int> converts implicitly.
std::from_chars(first, last, value) returns {ptr, ec}. The text is a complete valid int only if ec == std::errc{} AND ptr == last.
from_chars accepts a leading '-' but NOT '+', and reports overflow as std::errc::result_out_of_range - exactly the behavior the spec asks for.
safe_div: besides b == 0, INT_MIN / -1 overflows in C++ (undefined behavior!) - return nullopt for that too.
